_note: v12 (branch: LoRA capacity): v10.3 (text anchor, 3 validation splits; mean val HM 61.15%) with ONE change: LoRA on all 12 image-encoder blocks at rank 32 (alpha 64, so alpha/rank stays 2) instead of the last 8 at rank 16. Why: more adaptation capacity is the only image-side change that clearly helped (v5 -> v5.3, 4 blocks rank 8 -> 8 blocks rank 16: +5.7 val HM), while changes that pull the model back toward frozen CLIP (v10 image consistency, v10.2 EMA, v9 LoRA scale) did not. Seen accuracy after calibration is the bottleneck and seen errors are mostly right crop / wrong disease, an image-side problem. Risk: overfitting sooner (v5.3 peaked at epoch 6 vs v5's 13) and drifting from CLIP's image space that the unseen pairs rely on; the text anchor stays on. Same 3 splits as v10.3, so compare per split. Keep if mean validation HM beats v10.3's 61.15% by > 2 points.
_result: Not kept (below the 2-point bar). Mean validation HM 61.80% over 3 splits (epoch 11, gamma 0.08) vs v10.3 61.15% (+0.65); per split 58.09 / 65.03 / 62.27 vs 58.21 / 62.63 / 62.60, i.e. -0.1 / +2.4 / -0.3, so the gain is one split. More capacity raised val-seen (about 70-75% vs mid-60s) but not pseudo-unseen (flat or falling late in training, most on split 3), and the needed gamma kept rising (0.05 -> 0.09). Test (reported, not used to decide): HM 67.95% (v10.3 66.3%), seen 58.6% (55.1%), unseen 80.9% (83.3%), seen disease 62.7% (58.6%), seen crop 84.3%; uncalibrated seen 70.0%; AUSUC 0.574 (v10.3 0.562). Same pattern as v5.3: capacity buys seen accuracy, not unseen transfer. Needed grad_checkpointing_image (without it 5.9/6 GB and spilling); about 125 s per validation epoch, 165 s per refit epoch, 2 h 10 min in total.
title: lora_all_blocks

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: v12: all 12 blocks, rank 32, alpha 64 (alpha/rank 2 as before, so only capacity changes). About 4.7M adapter parameters vs 1.57M in v10.3 (3x). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat. v10.3: n_splits 1 -> 3 (seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2); selection uses the mean validation HM over splits, as in v4.2.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. v12: also on the image encoder (grad_checkpointing_image): with gradients through all 12 blocks at batch 64 the run filled 5.9 of 6 GB and spilled into shared memory (no epoch after 7 min). Recomputing activations in backward changes speed only, not results. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache.
